proposals.before: Subordinates Tian Xingshu and Yang Hengsheng charged the enemy line and killed several of their boldest leaders; the main force followed, the rebels broke and fled, and forty-seven stockades were destroyed.
proposals.after: His subordinate officers Tian Xingshu and Yang Hengsheng charged the enemy line and killed several of their boldest leaders; the main force followed, the rebels broke and fled, and forty-seven stockades were destroyed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 部將 marks them as his subordinate officers; English opens with bare 'Subordinates', obscuring the possessive link to Qijiang.

proposals.before: Changyou attacked from the southwest and Qijiang from the northeast, leveling all rebel encampments outside the walls.
proposals.after: Changyou attacked from the southwest and Qijiang from the northeast, leveling all the rebel encampments outside the city walls.
proposals.reason: Chinese 盡平城外賊屯 is 'leveled all rebel camps outside the city'; 平城 is verb+object, not a place name Pingcheng.

proposals.before: Shi Dakai broke out of Chongyi into Hunan; the Chenzhou and Guilin districts were all thrown into alarm, and Qijiang rushed to the defense.
proposals.after: Shi Dakai broke out of Chongyi into Hunan; the Chenzhou and Gui (Guiyang) districts were all thrown into alarm, and Qijiang rushed to the defense.
proposals.reason: Chinese 郴、桂 in a Hunan defense context denotes Chenzhou and Guiyang jurisdictions, not Guilin (桂林), which appears properly later when the campaign reaches Guangxi.

proposals.before: Shi Dakai fled from Chongyi into Hunan; all districts under Chen and Gui raised alarms, and Qijiang hurried to defend.
proposals.after: Shi Dakai fled from Chongyi into Hunan; all districts under Chen and Gui (Guiyang) raised alarms, and Qijiang hurried to defend.
proposals.reason: Literal already uses Chen and Gui; clarify that 桂 here is Hunan Guiyang jurisdiction, not Guilin (桂林).

proposals.before: Early in the Xianfeng reign he campaigned under Wang Zhen across Hengyang, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guilin, and rose by merit to subprefect.
proposals.after: Early in the Xianfeng reign he campaigned under Wang Zhen across Hengyang, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guiyang, and rose by merit to subprefect.
proposals.reason: Chinese 桂 in the Hunan campaign circuit 衡、永、郴、桂 abbreviates Guiyang (桂陽), not Guilin (桂林).

proposals.before: At the beginning of Xianfeng he followed Wang Zhen in campaigns through Hengyang, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guilin, and through accumulated merit was promoted to subprefect.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Xianfeng he followed Wang Zhen in campaigns through Hengyang, Yongzhou, Chenzhou, and Guiyang, and through accumulated merit was promoted to subprefect.
proposals.reason: Same 桂→桂陽 (Guiyang) error as in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: In 1856, at Tongcheng, Yunlan laid three ambushes, slew the rebel chief Zhang Yongzhong before his own lines, captured Lu Sanyuan, and took the city; he then routed the enemy again at Baiwan Bridge in Chongyang and was awarded the peacock feather.
proposals.after: In 1856, at Tongcheng, Yunlan laid three ambushes, slew the rebel chief Zhang Yongzhong before his own lines, captured Lu Sanyuan, and took the city; he then routed the enemy again at Bainí Bridge in Chongyang and was awarded the peacock feather.
proposals.reason: 白蜺橋 uses 蜺 (ní, 'rainbow'), not a wan/灣 reading; Baiwan misrenders the place name.

proposals.before: In 1863 he was sent to aid Guangdong, smashed the rebel nest at Shidang in Yangshan, accepted three thousand surrenders, and at Lianzhou captured the rebel chieftain Li Fuyou.
proposals.after: In 1863 he was sent to aid Guangdong, smashed the rebel nest at Shiying in Yangshan, accepted three thousand surrenders, and at Lianzhou captured the rebel chieftain Li Fuyou.
proposals.reason: 石塋 is Shiying (塋 yíng), not Shidang.

proposals.before: Yunlan hurried to Wuping with five hundred men, ran into the rebels, and was hopelessly outnumbered; Brigadiers He Shizhen and Wang Minggao and Vice Commander Lei Zhaoxiong were all killed in action.
proposals.after: Yunlan hurried to Wuping with five hundred men, ran into the rebels, and was hopelessly outnumbered; brigade commanders He Shizhen and Wang Minggao and vice commander Lei Zhaoxiong were all killed in action.
proposals.reason: Plural 'Brigadiers' fused onto only the first name; lowercase common nouns better match 總兵/副將 as office labels before the personal names.

proposals.before: In 1862, when Anhui Governor Li Xuyi was released from mourning and went home on leave, he recommended Xunfang as his replacement, and Xunfang was ordered to serve as acting governor.
proposals.after: In 1862, when Anhui Governor Li Xuyi, who had been ordered to remain in office despite mourning for his mother (奪情), asked leave to return home, he recommended Xunfang as his replacement, and Xunfang was ordered to serve as acting governor.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 母 and mistranslates 奪情 (court order to interrupt mourning and stay in office) as merely being 'released from mourning'.

proposals.before: Duolong'a and Bao Chao met the enemy at Songtingzi in Suzhou and routed them.
proposals.after: Duolong'a and Bao Chao met the enemy at Huatingzi in Susong and routed them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宿松 is Susong (Anhui), not Suzhou; 花亭子 is Huatingzi. Both idiomatic and literal misread the place.

proposals.before: Duolong'a and Bao Chao joined in attacking rebels at Songtingzi in Suzhou and defeated them.
proposals.after: Duolong'a and Bao Chao joined in attacking rebels at Huatingzi in Susong and defeated them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宿松 is Susong, not Suzhou; literal repeats the same place error.

proposals.before: That winter Governor Yang Yuebin of Shaanxi and Gansu requested Ningxue's transfer to Gansu; at Fancheng he ran into the mutiny of Bao Chao's Ting Corps.
proposals.after: That winter Governor-general Yang Yuebin of Shaanxi and Gansu requested Ningxue's transfer to Gansu; at Fancheng he ran into the mutiny of the Ting Corps.
proposals.reason: 陝甘總督 is Governor-general, not Governor; 霆軍 is the Ting Corps and need not insert Bao Chao into the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: Mourning honors were granted, and he was posthumously made a grand secretary of the Inner Court.
proposals.after: Mourning honors were granted, and he was posthumously made an academician of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is an academician/reader of the Grand Secretariat, not 大學士 (Grand Secretary).

proposals.before: Mourning favors were granted, and he was posthumously made a grand secretary of the Inner Court.
proposals.after: Mourning favors were granted, and he was posthumously made an academician of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation of 內閣學士 in the literal English.

proposals.before: He fell back to defend the city; after two days and nights of assault he stood on the wall and a bullet struck his left cheek.
proposals.after: He fell back to defend the city; after two days and nights of assault he stood among the parapets and a bullet struck his left cheek.
proposals.reason: 埤兒/埤堄 means parapet crenellations; "wall" is vaguer than the Chinese.

proposals.before: When Governor Wang Youqin of Zhejiang requested him for the relief of Zhejiang, Yuandu did not wait for orders, went home, raised eight thousand men as the Anyue Army.
proposals.after: When Governor Wang Youling of Zhejiang requested him for the relief of Zhejiang, Yuandu did not wait for orders, went home, raised eight thousand men as the Anyue Army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 王有齡 is Wang Youling (齡 líng); the idiomatic spelling Youqin misreads the given name.

proposals.before: When Zhejiang Governor Wang Youqin memorialized to transfer him to aid Zhejiang, Yuandu did not await orders, returned home to raise eight thousand braves, called the Anyue Army.
proposals.after: When Zhejiang Governor Wang Youling memorialized to transfer him to aid Zhejiang, Yuandu did not await orders, returned home to raise eight thousand braves, called the Anyue Army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 王有齡 is Wang Youling; literal English Youqin is a misreading of 齡.

proposals.before: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youqin died, Zuo Zongtang was appointed in his place.
proposals.after: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youling died, Zuo Zongtang was appointed in his place.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 王有齡 as Wang Youqin instead of Wang Youling.

proposals.before: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youqin died, an edict replaced him with Zuo Zongtang.
proposals.after: When Hangzhou fell and Wang Youling died, an edict replaced him with Zuo Zongtang.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 王有齡 as Wang Youqin instead of Wang Youling.

proposals.before: In 1860 Zeng Guofan directed operations in southern Anhui and transferred Yuandu to the Ningchi-Taizhou intendant post to defend Huizhou.
proposals.after: In 1860 Zeng Guofan directed operations in southern Anhui and transferred Yuandu to the Ningchi-Tai circuit intendant post to defend Huizhou.
proposals.reason: 寧池太道 is the Ning-Chi-Tai (Ningguo–Chizhou–Taiping) circuit, not Taizhou; Taizhou invents a wrong place-name.

proposals.before: In the tenth year Zeng Guofan directed the army in southern Anhui and transferred Yuandu to the Ningchi-Taizhou circuit in Anhui to defend Huizhou.
proposals.after: In the tenth year Zeng Guofan directed the army in southern Anhui and transferred Yuandu to the Ningchi-Tai circuit in Anhui to defend Huizhou.
proposals.reason: 寧池太道 denotes Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping; rendering 太 as Taizhou is incorrect.
